About.TITLE: About
About.DESCRIPTION: Keydra is a web-based management console for key-value servers: Redis, Valkey and the RESP-compatible forks, Aerospike and TiKV.
About.NAME: Name
About.LOAD_ERROR_BODY: Keydra could not be reached, or refused the request. Try again; if it keeps happening, an administrator can check the server log.
About.LOGS_PLAIN: Written for a person to read

Access.TITLE: Access
Access.INTRO: Who may do what, and on which servers. A person holds a role on a scope; nothing takes access away, so an empty cell is the whole of a refusal.
Access.MATRIX_DESCRIPTION: What every account adds up to, following the groups people are in and the groups servers are in. A filled label was granted here; an outlined one arrived from a group above.
Access.MATRIX_FAILED: Could not work out who holds what
Access.NO_USERS_BODY: An account lets somebody sign in and see nothing. Access arrives as a grant.
Access.REMOVE_USER_BODY: {{name}} will no longer be able to sign in, and their grants go with them.
Access.PASSWORD_UNCHANGED: Leave empty to keep the current password.
Access.ENABLED_HELP: A disabled account cannot sign in, and keeps its grants for when it is enabled again.
Access.NO_GROUPS_BODY: A group is what keeps the grants short: grant the group once and everybody in it holds the role.
Access.REMOVE_GROUP_BODY: Everybody in {{name}} loses whatever it was granted.
Access.SERVER_GROUPS_FAILED: Could not load the server groups
Access.NO_SERVER_GROUPS_BODY: A server group is what a grant points at, so people get access to a set of servers rather than one at a time.
Access.REMOVE_SERVER_GROUP_BODY: Grants on {{name}} go with it. The servers themselves are untouched.
Access.NO_PARENT: Nothing — it stands on its own
Access.PARENT_HELP: A grant on the parent reaches everything in here too.
Access.REMOVE_ROLE_BODY: Every grant that named {{name}} goes with it.
Access.BUILT_IN_HELP: What the built-in roles carry is defined in Keydra itself and rewritten at every start, so it cannot be edited here.
Access.NO_GRANTS_BODY: Nobody can reach anything until a grant says so.
Access.PREFER_GROUPS: Granting a group is usually the one to reach for; a person's access then follows from who they work with.
Access.NAME: Name
Access.NO_PROVIDERS_BODY: Everybody signs in with a password Keydra keeps. Add a provider and they can use the account they already have.
Access.REMOVE_PROVIDER_BODY: Nobody will be able to sign in through {{name}} any more. The accounts it created stay, and keep their grants.
Access.KIND_OIDC: OpenID Connect — Keycloak, Entra, Google, Okta, Auth0
Access.PROVIDER_KEY_HELP: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. It appears in the redirect URI, so it cannot be changed later.
Access.ISSUER_HELP: Keydra fetches the discovery document from here when you save, and remembers where the endpoints are.
Access.SECRET_HELP: Stored encrypted and never sent back.
Access.SECRET_UNCHANGED: One is stored. Leave empty to keep it.
Access.SUBJECT_CLAIM_HELP: What identifies somebody for good — sub for OpenID Connect, id at GitHub. Not the username: usernames change.
Access.GROUPS_CLAIM_HELP: Leave empty if the provider sends no groups.
Access.REDIRECT_URI_HELP: Give this to the provider exactly as it appears. A first attempt is usually refused because it does not match.
Access.PROVIDER_ENABLED_HELP: A disabled provider disappears from the login page and stops accepting anybody.
Access.AUTO_CREATE_HELP: Off means only people an administrator has already prepared may sign in. Either way they hold nothing until somebody grants it.
Access.MAP_GROUPS_HELP: Membership of a mapped group is replaced at every sign-in by what the provider says. Groups nobody mapped are left alone.
Access.MAP_FAILED: Could not draw who reaches what
Access.MAP_DESCRIPTION: Every way access reached whoever is selected, read across: from them, through the groups that carried it, to what it was granted on.
Access.PERMISSIONS_HELP: Down the side is what is acted on, across the top is what may be done to it. An empty cell means there is no such permission, not that it was withheld.
Access.HOLDS_NOTHING_BODY: They can sign in and see nothing. Grant them a role, or put them in a group that already has one.
Access.INVITATION_EXPLAINED: Keydra emails an invitation. The person sets their own password, so nobody else ever knows it.
Access.INVITE_LINK_BODY: Keydra could not email it, so give it to them another way. It works once and is not shown again.
Access.POLICY_INTRO: What this instance asks of everybody who signs in with a password here. Accounts that sign in through an identity provider are not covered — that provider decides how its people prove who they are.
Access.POLICY_FAILED: The sign-in policy could not be read
Access.POLICY_PAIR_YOURS: Pair an authenticator with your own account
Access.REQUIRE_SECOND_FACTOR_HELP: An account without one can sign in and reach nothing but its own enrolment until it pairs an authenticator.
Access.POLICY_OWING_one: {{count}} account has not paired an authenticator
Access.POLICY_OWING_other: {{count}} accounts have not paired an authenticator
Access.POLICY_OWING_BODY: They keep working until the requirement is on. After that they can sign in, and reach nothing else until they enrol.
Access.POLICY_ALL_ENROLLED: Every account that this reaches has paired an authenticator
Access.POLICY_CHANGED_BY_NOBODY: somebody who is no longer here
Access.POLICY_CONFIRM_BODY_one: {{count}} account has no authenticator paired. It will be able to sign in and to reach nothing but its own enrolment until it pairs one. You can turn this off again at any time.
Access.POLICY_CONFIRM_BODY_other: {{count}} accounts have no authenticator paired. They will be able to sign in and to reach nothing but their own enrolment until they pair one. You can turn this off again at any time.

Acl.TITLE: Target users
Acl.DESCRIPTION: The users this target itself knows about, and what each of them may reach.
Acl.NO_HASHES: Password hashes are never shown here. A browser has no use for one; an attacker does.
Acl.RULES_HELP: The target's own rule syntax, passed through unaltered — for example: on ~cache:* +@read +@write
Acl.DELETE_BODY: Anything authenticating as {{name}} will stop being able to reach this target.
Acl.LOAD_ERROR: The target's users could not be read

Alerts.DELETE_BODY: “{{name}}” and everything it has said will be removed. Nothing on the target changes.
Alerts.DELIVERIES_EMPTY_BODY: Add an address and a firing rule reaches it — an HTTP endpoint covers Slack, Teams, Discord and anything that accepts a webhook.
Alerts.DELIVERIES_ERROR: The deliveries could not be read
Alerts.DELIVERY_ADMIN_ONLY: Only an administrator can add somewhere to send alerts.
Alerts.DELIVERY_DELETE_BODY: “{{name}}” will be removed. Rules pointing at it have to be sent somewhere else first.
Alerts.DESCRIPTION: Conditions worth being told about. Writing a rule is how a target gets watched when nobody is looking at it.
Alerts.EMPTY_BODY: A rule watches one reading of one target and says so when it crosses a line — in Keydra, and anywhere else you point it.
Alerts.EMPTY_UNPRIVILEGED: Rules about a target need permission on that target.
Alerts.ENABLED_HINT: An enabled rule keeps its target sampled, whether or not anybody has the dashboard open.
Alerts.FOR_HINT: Without this, every scrape spike is an alert — and an alert that has cried wolf twice gets muted, which is worse than not having one.
Alerts.FROM_HINT: Most servers refuse a message without one.
Alerts.HISTORY_EMPTY_BODY: Only transitions are recorded: a rule that has been firing since Tuesday appears once, and clearing appears too.
Alerts.HISTORY_ERROR: The history could not be read
Alerts.IN_APP_ONLY_HINT: The event is recorded and shown here either way. A delivery is the second copy, for the hours when nobody has Keydra open.
Alerts.KIND_EMAIL_HINT: Through a mail server you nominate. The subject names the target, because that is what somebody sees first.
Alerts.KIND_WEBHOOK_HINT: A JSON body naming the rule, the target and the reading. This is how Slack, Teams, Discord and most on-call tools take a message.
Alerts.LOAD_ERROR: The rules could not be read
Alerts.METRIC_HINT_HIT_RATIO_PERCENT: Absent while nothing has been looked up: no hits and no misses is not a ratio of zero.
Alerts.METRIC_HINT_MEMORY_FILL_PERCENT: Absent on a target with no memory ceiling, where “full” has nothing to be measured against.
Alerts.METRIC_HINT_NO_ANSWER: The target stopped replying. The one condition that is the absence of a reading rather than a reading.
Alerts.METRIC_HINT_UPTIME_SECONDS: Written as “below 60 seconds”, which is how a restart is noticed after the fact.
Alerts.NAME: Name
Alerts.NO_TARGETS: You cannot write rules about any target yet.
Alerts.SECRET_KEPT: Stored. Leave empty to keep it.
Alerts.TITLE: Alerts
Alerts.UNIT_PER_MINUTE: Per minute, worked out from two readings.
Alerts.URL_HINT: Kept encrypted and never shown again. A webhook address carries its authorisation in its path: whoever holds the string can post as Keydra.
Alerts.URL_KEPT: Stored — at {{host}}. Leave empty to keep it.
Alerts.BASIS_HELP: A fixed amount needs somebody to know what this server usually does. Comparing with the past does not, and stays right when the service grows.
Alerts.COMPARE_WITH_HELP: An hour of readings from then, averaged. A single reading from the past is a spike as easily as it is normal.
Alerts.SHARE_HELP: Per cent. 140 is 40% above what the metric read then; 60 is 40% below it.
Alerts.KIND_TELEGRAM_HINT: A bot you create with BotFather, posting into one chat. Use this rather than an HTTP endpoint when the team reads Telegram.
Alerts.KIND_SLACK_HINT: A bot token and a channel by name, so the channel can be changed without issuing a new address. An incoming webhook works too, as an HTTP endpoint.
Alerts.KIND_WHATSAPP_HINT: Through the WhatsApp Cloud API, from a number registered with it. The recipient must have messaged that number, or be on its test list.
Alerts.API_TOKEN_TELEGRAM_HINT: The token BotFather gave the bot. Kept encrypted and never shown again.
Alerts.API_TOKEN_SLACK_HINT: A bot token with chat:write, from the app’s OAuth page. The bot has to be in the channel before it can post there. Kept encrypted and never shown again.
Alerts.API_TOKEN_WHATSAPP_HINT: An access token from the Meta for Developers dashboard. Kept encrypted and never shown again.
Alerts.CHAT_ID_HINT: The chat id the bot posts into. A group id begins with a minus sign.
Alerts.CHANNEL_HINT: With or without the hash — #alerts and alerts both work.
Alerts.PHONE_NUMBER_HINT: In full international form, including the country code.
Alerts.SENDER_ID_HINT: The phone number id the message is sent from. The Cloud API dashboard shows it beside the number itself.
Alerts.NO_DELIVERIES: No destinations are configured. The rule still records what it sees and shows it in the application.
Alerts.SENDS_TO_HINT_one: Announced in {{count}} place, as well as in the application.
Alerts.SENDS_TO_HINT_other: Announced in {{count}} places, as well as in the application.
Alerts.INSTANCE_NOTICES_HELP: An identity provider or a backup destination that stops answering announces itself here — once when it stops, once when it starts again.
Alerts.INSTANCE_NOTICES_NONE: Nothing is told. The instances page still says what answered and when it was found out.

Analysis.TITLE: Keyspace analysis
Analysis.CENSUS_one: Every one of the {{count}} keys was measured.
Analysis.SAMPLE: {{sampled}} of {{total}} keys measured — the proportions hold, the totals do not.
Analysis.NEVER_EXPIRES_TITLE: {{percent}}% of the sampled keys have no expiry
Analysis.NEVER_EXPIRES_BODY: That is {{bytes}} the server will never release on its own. A cache whose entries never expire is not a cache — it is a growing table.
Analysis.EMPTY_BODY: This database is empty, so there is no memory to account for.
Analysis.LOAD_ERROR: The keyspace could not be measured

Approvals.APPROVED: Approved; the operation is running on {{name}}
Approvals.DECLINE_REASON_HELP: The person who asked reads this, so say what would change your answer
Approvals.DESCRIPTION: Operations on targets that nobody empties on their own, waiting for a second person
Approvals.LOAD_ERROR: The requests could not be read
Approvals.NONE_BODY: An operation appears here when it would empty a target that asks for two people. Turn that on for a target from its connection profile.
Approvals.TABLE_LABEL: Operations waiting for a second person
Approvals.TITLE: Approvals
Approvals.YOURS_HELP: You asked for this one, so somebody else has to agree to it

Audit.DESCRIPTION: What has been done, and by whom. Changes are recorded, reads are not.
Audit.EMPTY_BODY: Operations that change something appear here. Reads are not recorded — a log of every page view buries the entries somebody will come looking for.
Audit.LOAD_ERROR: The audit log could not be read
Audit.TITLE: Audit log
Audit.WHOLE_ALERT_INSTANCE_NOTICES: Where Keydra's own troubles go changed

Backups.ACCESS_KEY_HELP: Leave empty to use the machine’s own credentials — an instance role or a mounted service account.
Backups.CONNECTION_DESCRIPTION: What has been taken of {{name}}, and putting one back.
Backups.DESCRIPTION: Where backups go. A bucket name and a key live here once, rather than once per schedule that uses them.
Backups.DESTINATION_INTRO: What kind of place it is, where it is, and how to get in. Secrets are stored encrypted and never shown again.
Backups.DIFFERENT_TARGET_BODY: It was taken from {{from}} and you are restoring it into {{into}}. That is sometimes exactly right — copying production into staging — and sometimes the mistake nobody notices until later.
Backups.DIFFERENT_TARGET_TITLE: This backup came from somewhere else
Backups.DIRECTORY_HELP: Inside the backup root this deployment is configured with. Leave empty to use the root itself.
Backups.EMPTY_BODY: A backup written next to the application is not a backup: the one failure it exists for is the machine going away, and that copy goes with it. Add somewhere else — a bucket, an SFTP drop, or anything with an address.
Backups.EMPTY_TITLE: Nowhere to back up to yet
Backups.ENABLED_HELP: Turn this off to stop new backups going here without forgetting how to reach it.
Backups.ENDPOINT_HELP: Leave empty for AWS itself. Anything else — MinIO, R2, Spaces — needs its address here.
Backups.FTPS_HELP: Only if the server offers it; plain FTP sends the password in the clear.
Backups.KIND_AZURE_BLOB_HELP: A container in an Azure storage account.
Backups.KIND_CUSTOM_HELP: Anywhere reachable by an endpoint address — a message queue, an HTTP endpoint, a mail server, another storage service. Write only: a backup can be sent here and cannot be listed, restored or pruned.
Backups.KIND_FTP_HELP: Plain FTP, or FTPS where the server offers it.
Backups.KIND_LOCAL_HELP: A directory on the machine Keydra runs on, which is also how a mounted share is reached. Convenient, and no protection against that machine going away.
Backups.KIND_S3_HELP: S3 and everything that speaks its API: MinIO, Cloudflare R2, DigitalOcean Spaces.
Backups.KIND_SFTP_HELP: Over SSH, with a password or a private key.
Backups.LIST_ERROR: The destination could not be read
Backups.LOAD_ERROR: The destinations could not be read
Backups.NAME: Name
Backups.NONE_YET_BODY: Take one now, or arrange it under Scheduled work so it happens without anybody watching.
Backups.NO_DESTINATIONS_BODY: An administrator adds a destination under Backups, and this page fills up.
Backups.NO_ENCRYPTION_BODY: A backup is every key and every value. Without a passphrase it lands as a plain compressed file wherever it goes, and "the bucket is private" is a sentence about access control rather than about what is in the file.
Backups.NO_ENCRYPTION_TITLE: Backups sent here are readable by whoever holds them
Backups.PASSPHRASE_HELP: When there is one, everything sent here is encrypted before it leaves. Leave empty to keep what is stored.
Backups.PASSPHRASE_WARNING_BODY: Backups written with it cannot be read without it — not by anyone, Keydra included. That is what it is for, and it is also how a backup is lost.
Backups.PASSPHRASE_WARNING_TITLE: Write this passphrase down somewhere else
Backups.PATH_STYLE_HELP: Needed by nearly everything that is not AWS. Without it a MinIO on an IP address is looked up as bucket.10.0.0.4, and the failure reads as a DNS problem.
Backups.PRIVATE_HALF_BODY: This is the only half that can read the backups, and it exists nowhere but on this screen. Keydra did not store it and cannot show it again.
Backups.PRIVATE_HALF_TITLE: Copy this now — it will not be shown again
Backups.PRIVATE_KEY_HELP: Used for this restore and kept nowhere — not stored, not logged.
Backups.RECIPIENT_BODY: It holds only the half that encrypts, so it can write a backup every night and cannot open one — and neither can anybody who takes this server. Restoring asks for the other half.
Backups.RECIPIENT_HELP: The half that only encrypts. Paste keys you already have, or generate a pair below — each one is somebody who will be able to open these backups.
Backups.RECIPIENT_TITLE: Keydra will not be able to read these backups
Backups.REMOVE_BODY: Keydra forgets how to reach “{{name}}”. The backups already there stay where they are.
Backups.REPLACE: Overwrite keys that are already there
Backups.REPLACE_HELP: Off by default. A restore usually goes into a store that has moved on since, and quietly overwriting the newer data is the one outcome nobody wants by default.
Backups.SAVE_FAILED: The destination could not be saved
Backups.SEALED_TO_KEY_BODY: This backup was encrypted to a key Keydra does not hold the other half of. Paste it to restore, or read the file outside Keydra with scripts/keydra-decrypt.py.
Backups.SECRET_HELP: Leave empty to keep what is stored. Nothing can read a secret back to show it here.
Backups.SECRET_NEW_HELP: Stored encrypted, and never written to disk.
Backups.SERVICE_ACCOUNT_KEY_HELP: The whole JSON key file. Stored encrypted, and never written to disk. Leave empty to use the machine’s own credentials.
Backups.STORED: stored — leave empty to keep it
Backups.TAKE_FAILED: The backup could not be taken
Backups.TAKE_INTRO: Streams the keyspace into a compressed file and sends it to {{name}}.
Backups.TITLE: Backups
Backups.TUNNEL_HELP: A jump host, for a drop or a store that is not reachable from where Keydra runs. Only kinds named by a host and a port can be tunnelled; the public clouds are named by an address inside a certificate.
Backups.WRITE_ONLY_BODY: This kind of destination can be written to and not read back, so what is already there cannot be shown and cannot be restored from here. Backups still go to it.
Backups.RECIPIENT_LATER_TITLE: A key added later opens later backups
Backups.RECIPIENT_LATER_BODY: A file carries the keys it was written to, and nothing rewrites a file that has already been sent. Backups taken before a key is added can still only be opened by the keys they name.

CommandWatch.TITLE: Live commands
CommandWatch.DESCRIPTION: Everything this target is being asked to do, as it happens.
CommandWatch.FILTER: Filter by command, argument or client
CommandWatch.IDLE_BODY: Watching copies every command this server runs to your browser, so it is off until you ask for it. It costs the server work while it is on.
CommandWatch.WAITING_BODY: Nothing has run yet. Every command any client sends will appear here.
CommandWatch.DROPPED_one: {{count}} command was not shown because they arrived faster than they could be read.
CommandWatch.DROPPED_other: {{count}} commands were not shown because they arrived faster than they could be read.
CommandWatch.NO_CONNECTION_BODY: Open live commands from a connection to watch it.

Connections.CONSOLE_ALLOWED: Commands the console may run here
Connections.CONSOLE_ALLOWED_HELP: These are refused on every target by default, because running the console is not the same as administering the server. Allowing one here allows it here only. Commands that would break Keydra's own connection to a server are not offered, because that is the same wherever the server is.
Connections.DELETE_BODY: "{{name}}" will be removed. Data on the target server is not affected.
Connections.DESCRIPTION: Saved Redis, Valkey, KeyDB, Dragonfly and Garnet targets. Status refreshes automatically.
Connections.EMPTY_BODY: Add a Redis, Valkey, KeyDB, Dragonfly or Garnet target to start browsing it.
Connections.GUARDED: Ask for this target's name before emptying it
Connections.GUARDED_HELP: Purging, deleting a selection, importing over what is there and migrating into this target will refuse unless its name is typed. Turn this on for a server whose data somebody would miss.
Connections.LOAD_ERROR_BODY: Keydra could not be reached, or refused the request. Try again; if it keeps happening, an administrator can check the server log.
Connections.MANAGE_SERVER_GROUPS: Create one on the Access page
Connections.NAME: Name
Connections.NAMESPACE_HELP: Which Aerospike namespace to read. Named rather than numbered, which is why it is not the database above — a namespace is configured on the server, so this has to be one that exists there
Connections.NO_MATCH_BODY: No saved connection matches the filter.
Connections.NO_SERVER_GROUPS_BODY: Server groups are what grants point at, so people reach a set of servers rather than one at a time.
Connections.PASSWORD_HELP: Leave empty if the target requires no password.
Connections.PASSWORD_KEEP_HELP: A password is stored. Leave empty to keep it, or type a new one to replace it.
Connections.PASTE_URL_HELP: Optional. Paste the redis:// or rediss:// address a provider gave you and the fields below fill themselves.
Connections.PASTE_URL_UNREADABLE: Not an address Keydra recognises. Fill the fields below instead.
Connections.REQUIRES_APPROVAL_HELP: An operation that could empty this target is recorded and waits for somebody else who holds the same permission. Never the person who asked for it.
Connections.SECRET_KEPT: Stored — leave empty to keep it
Connections.SERVER_GROUPS_HELP: A grant on a group reaches everything in it, including the groups inside it — so a server in `production` is reached by a grant on `production`, and one in a group beneath it is reached by the same grant. A target in no group is visible only to people granted on it directly, or over Keydra itself.
Connections.SERVER_HELP: Which server this target runs. They all speak the same protocol, so Keydra reads this from the server once it answers — saying it here is what lets the catalog show the right mark before that.
Connections.TEST_FAILED: The target could not be reached
Connections.TITLE: Connections
Connections.TLS_CA_HELP: The authority that signed this target's certificate, as PEM. Leave it empty to trust the authorities the runtime already trusts, which is right for a managed target and rarely right for one inside a company.
Connections.TLS_CLIENT_KEY_HELP: PEM, in either PKCS#1 or PKCS#8 form. A key protected by a passphrase needs the passphrase below.
Connections.TLS_KEY_PASSPHRASE_HELP: Only for a key that is protected. A passphrase given for a key that is not is refused when this is saved rather than ignored.
Connections.TLS_KEY_PASSPHRASE_KEEP_HELP: A passphrase is stored. Leave this empty to keep it.
Connections.TLS_KEY_STORED: A key is stored. Leave this empty to keep it.
Connections.TUNNEL: Reach this target through an SSH tunnel
Connections.TUNNEL_ANY_KEY: This tunnel accepts any host key
Connections.TUNNEL_ANY_KEY_BODY: Anything answering on {{name}}’s address can present itself as the jump host, and everything this target sends goes through it. Pin its key under Tunnels.
Connections.TUNNEL_HELP: Described once under Tunnels and pointed at from here, so one jump host is one key rather than one per target.
Connections.TUNNEL_NONE_CONFIGURED: No tunnel is configured yet. An administrator adds one under Tunnels.

Console.CLEAR: Clear the transcript and forget the history
Console.DESCRIPTION: Run commands against this target. History survives the session.
Console.DISCONNECTED_BODY: Reload the page to start another one.
Console.EMPTY_BODY: Anything the server accepts will run here. {{count}} commands are refused, either because they never return on a shared connection or because they would stall the server.
Console.INPUT_PLACEHOLDER: Type a command, press Tab to complete, ↑ for history
Console.NO_CONNECTION_BODY: Open a console from a connection to run commands against it.
Console.REASON_BLOCKS_THE_SERVER: Blocks the server for as long as the keyspace is large
Console.REASON_CHANGES_THE_SERVER: Changes what the server is, or stops it
Console.REASON_COPIES_ELSEWHERE: Copies keys to any host, past every visibility rule and every audit entry
Console.REASON_CREATES_AN_IDENTITY: Creates an identity on the target that Keydra cannot show, filter or revoke
Console.REASON_CUTS_OTHERS_OFF: Stops or cuts off everybody else using the target
Console.REASON_DESERIALISES: Deserialises a value somebody else shaped, which has been an execution path before
Console.REASON_ERASES_EVIDENCE: Erases the record of what has been slow, which is evidence
Console.REASON_REARRANGES_A_CLUSTER: Rearranges or resets a cluster from a console meant for one node
Console.REASON_REPLICATION_INTERNALS: Streams the whole dataset down a shared connection and does not give it back
Console.REASON_WRITES_A_FILE: Writes a file wherever the server process may write
Console.REFUSED: The console does not run {{command}} — it would never return on a shared connection, lock the server, or change what that connection is for everybody using it.
Console.TITLE: Console

CreateKey.TITLE: New key
CreateKey.DESCRIPTION: A key exists because something was written to it, so this creates the key by writing its first value.
CreateKey.KEY_HELP: Namespaces are a convention, not a feature: a colon in the name is what puts a key in a folder.
CreateKey.TTL_HELP: Leave empty for a key that does not expire.
CreateKey.FAILED: The key could not be created

Failure.GONE: This is no longer here. It may have been deleted since the page was opened.
Failure.NOT_ALLOWED: You do not have permission to see this. An administrator can grant it.
Failure.REFUSED: Keydra could not answer that request. Try again; if it keeps happening, an administrator can check the server log.
Failure.SERVER: The server ran into a problem. Try again; if it keeps happening, an administrator can check the server log.
Failure.SIGNED_OUT: Your session has ended. Sign in again to carry on.
Failure.TOO_MANY: Too many requests at once. Wait a moment, then try again.
Failure.TOO_SLOW: The server took too long to answer. Try again, or narrow what you asked for.
Failure.UNREACHABLE: Keydra could not be reached. Check that it is running, then try again.

ImportKeys.TITLE: Import keys
ImportKeys.DESCRIPTION: Restores a file taken with export. Keys already on this target are left alone unless replacing is asked for.
ImportKeys.NOT_AN_EXPORT: That file is not a Keydra export: an export is a list of keys.
ImportKeys.REPLACE_HELP: Without this, a key already on this target is left as it is and counted as skipped.

Instances.CHANGES_NONE: Nothing has changed since Keydra started keeping this. A row appears here when something starts or stops answering, rather than every time it is asked.
Instances.CHECK_TOO_SOON: Everything was checked a moment ago. Try again shortly.
Instances.CHORES_STOPPED: Nothing is doing the scheduled work
Instances.CHORES_STOPPED_BODY: No instance has held the chores since {{since}}, so schedules, alert rules and sweeps are not running. Check that at least one instance is not draining.
Instances.DEP_NOTE_MAIL_OFF: Not configured; invitations and mail alerts cannot be sent
Instances.DEP_NOTE_METRICS_HISTORY_OFF: Not configured; readings are kept in memory and lost on restart
Instances.DEP_NOTE_SHARED_STORE_LOCAL: Cached in this process; set keydra.store.url to share it between instances
Instances.DESCRIPTION: How Keydra itself is doing: which instances are running, which of them does the work that must happen once, and whether they can reach what they rest on.
Instances.DRAIN_BODY: It stops reporting itself ready, so nothing new is sent to it, and it gives up the work that must happen once. Everything it is already holding stays with it until you stop it.
Instances.DRAIN_FAILED: Could not change whether that instance is in service
Instances.DRAIN_ONLY_ONE: It is the only instance running, so nothing will do the scheduled work until it is put back into service or another instance starts.
Instances.LOAD_ERROR: Keydra could not report on itself
Instances.NONE_BODY: Something answered this request, so at least one is running — which means the roster is not being written. Check that Keydra can reach its database.
Instances.TITLE: Instances
Instances.WATCHING: Targets this instance holds clients for, as of its last beat
Instances.WATCHING_NONE: None. It has opened no client to a target since it started, or a balancer has stopped sending it work.

Invitation.TITLE: Choose a password
Invitation.SUBTITLE: For the account {{username}}.
Invitation.MISMATCH: The two passwords are not the same.
Invitation.FAILED: The password could not be set. The link may have been used in another tab.
Invitation.REFUSED_USED: This link has already been used.
Invitation.REFUSED_UNKNOWN: This link is not one Keydra recognises.
Invitation.REFUSED_HELP: Ask an administrator to send a new one.
Invitation.FORGOTTEN_BODY: Enter your username. If there is an account, a link to set a new password is emailed to it.
Invitation.FORGOTTEN_SENT: If there is such an account, a link is on its way.

KeyBrowser.AT_LIMIT_HELP: This page holds as many keys as it safely can. Narrow the filter to see different ones.
KeyBrowser.COPY_REFUSED: A key with that name already exists. Tick overwrite to replace it.
KeyBrowser.DELETE_BODY_MANY: {{count}} keys will be deleted from the target. This cannot be undone.
KeyBrowser.DELETE_BODY_ONE: "{{name}}" will be deleted from the target. This cannot be undone.
KeyBrowser.DESCRIPTION: Keys stream in as the server scans, so results appear before the walk finishes.
KeyBrowser.DESTINATION_REPLACE: Overwrite the destination if it already exists
KeyBrowser.EMPTY_BODY: Nothing in this namespace matches the current filter.
KeyBrowser.EMPTY_TARGET_BODY: Nothing has been written to it yet, or everything written has expired.
KeyBrowser.FOUND_TRUNCATED: first {{count}} keys — refine the filter to narrow it down
KeyBrowser.FOUND_TRUNCATED_HELP: Only the first {{count}} keys were listed. Narrow the filter to see the rest.
KeyBrowser.KEYSPACE_ANNOUNCE_FAILED: The target would not change that setting: {{reason}}. A managed server often refuses it; ask whoever runs it.
KeyBrowser.KEYSPACE_SILENT_BODY: This target does not announce its own changes, so this list refreshes only when Keydra changes something. Announcing adds {{setting}} to notify-keyspace-events, keeping whatever it already said, and costs the server one message per write.
KeyBrowser.KEYSPACE_SILENT_BODY_READONLY: This target does not announce its own changes, so this list refreshes only when Keydra changes something. Ask somebody who can change this target's settings to turn announcements on.
KeyBrowser.KEYSPACE_SILENT_TITLE: Changes made outside Keydra are not shown
KeyBrowser.LOAD_ERROR_BODY: Keydra could not be reached, or refused the request. Try again; if it keeps happening, an administrator can check the server log.
KeyBrowser.PURGE_ALL_BODY: This empties the target completely. Deleted keys cannot be brought back, so type the target’s name to confirm.
KeyBrowser.PURGE_ALL_TITLE: Delete every key on this target?
KeyBrowser.PURGE_NAMESPACE_BODY_PARTIAL_one: This removes at least {{count}} key from this target — the tree counts from a sample, so there may be more. Deleted keys cannot be brought back.
KeyBrowser.PURGE_NAMESPACE_BODY_PARTIAL_other: This removes at least {{count}} keys from this target — the tree counts from a sample, so there may be more. Deleted keys cannot be brought back.
KeyBrowser.PURGE_NAMESPACE_BODY_one: This removes {{count}} key from this target. Deleted keys cannot be brought back.
KeyBrowser.PURGE_NAMESPACE_BODY_other: This removes {{count}} keys from this target. Deleted keys cannot be brought back.
KeyBrowser.RENAME_REFUSED: A key with that name already exists. Tick overwrite to replace it.
KeyBrowser.TITLE: Key browser
KeyBrowser.TOGGLE_TREE: Show or hide the namespace tree
KeyBrowser.TREE_COUNT_PARTIAL: At least this many. The tree counts from a sample rather than walking the whole keyspace, so each level is counted separately and none of these totals is final
KeyBrowser.TREE_EMPTY_BODY: This target is empty, so there are no namespaces to walk.
KeyBrowser.TREE_MORE: and {{count}} more — use the search box
KeyBrowser.TREE_SAMPLED: These namespaces come from a sample of the keyspace, so there may be others that are not shown.
KeyBrowser.TTL_FAILED: The key was created, but its expiry could not be set

Login.TITLE: Sign in to Keydra
Login.SUBTITLE: Use the account an administrator gave you.
Login.PRODUCT_BLURB: Keydra is a web console for Redis, Valkey, Aerospike and TiKV: browse keys, watch commands, run a console and manage a fleet of servers from one place.
Login.FOOTER_NOTE: Ask an administrator if you need an account.
Login.SETUP_SUBTITLE: This instance has no accounts yet. The first one you make is its administrator.
Login.PASSWORD_MISMATCH: The two passwords are not the same.
Login.TERMS_BODY: Keydra is software somebody runs themselves, and this is somebody's instance of it. Whoever operates it decides the terms on which you use it and what the servers behind it hold — Keydra's own licence covers the software, not this deployment. Ask whoever gave you the address.
Login.PRIVACY_BODY: Keydra keeps your username, whatever your provider tells it about you, and a record of the changes you make. It sends nothing anywhere: there is no telemetry and no third party. What it stores lives in the database of this instance, and whoever operates that decides how long it is kept.
Login.UNREACHABLE: Keydra did not answer. It may be restarting — try again in a moment.
Login.FAILED: Keydra could not complete the sign-in. Ask an administrator to check its logs.
Login.THROTTLED: Too many sign-in attempts. Wait a few minutes and try again.
Login.SECOND_FACTOR_HELP: The six digits your authenticator is showing, or one of your recovery codes.
Login.SECOND_FACTOR_WRONG: That code was not right. Check the current one, or use a recovery code.

Migrate.DELETE_SOURCE: Remove each key from this server once the other one has it
Migrate.DELETE_SOURCE_HELP: Turns the copy into a move. Only keys the destination accepted are removed.
Migrate.DESCRIPTION: Keydra reads from this target and writes to the other one, a batch at a time, so the two servers do not have to be able to reach each other.
Migrate.ENDED_SHORT: {{missing, number}} were not found — a key can expire or be deleted while a walk is running
Migrate.NO_TARGETS: No other target is answering. Add a connection, or check that one is up.
Migrate.PATTERN_HELP: A glob, for example user:*. Everything it matches is walked with SCAN, so a large keyspace is never held in memory.
Migrate.PREPARING_HINT: Looking for the keys that match
Migrate.REPLACE_HELP: Without this, a key already on the destination is left as it is and counted as skipped.
Migrate.SCOPE_PATTERN: Keys matching a pattern I type
Migrate.SCOPE_SELECTION_one: The {{count}} key ticked in the list
Migrate.SCOPE_SELECTION_other: The {{count}} keys ticked in the list
Migrate.TITLE: Move keys to another server
Migrate.TYPE_HELP: Narrowed while the keyspace is walked, so keys of other types are never read. Useful when the destination does not hold every type the source does
Migrate.PREFIX_HELP: Keys are written under the names they already have
Migrate.PREFIX_EXAMPLE: {{before}} is written as {{after}}. A key without the prefix is written unchanged
Migrate.RATE_LIMIT_NONE: As fast as the link allows
Migrate.RATE_LIMIT_HELP: A ceiling, for a migration running against a server somebody else is using
Migrate.SCRIPT: Decide each key with a script
Migrate.SCRIPT_HELP: Lua. `key.name` and `key.ttlMillis` are given; return nil to leave a key behind, a table like { name = ..., ttlMillis = ... } to change it, or true to move it as it is. Runs inside Keydra, so it needs script:run on the instance

Migrations.TITLE: Migrations
Migrations.EMPTY_BODY: Start a migration from a target’s key browser and it will appear here, whichever target it came from.
Migrations.LOAD_ERROR: The jobs could not be read
Migrations.INTERRUPTED_HINT: Keydra stopped while this was running. What had already been written is written.
Migrations.NO_MATCHES_BODY: Nothing here was moved between those targets, or nothing is in that state.
Migrations.RESUMED_HINT_one: The instance running this went away, so another one picked it up and started walking the keyspace again. The counters here are the current attempt's; keys already moved were not moved twice.
Migrations.RESUMED_HINT_other: The instance running this went away {{count}} times, and another one picked it up each time. The counters here are the current attempt's; keys already moved were not moved twice.

Monitoring.TITLE: Monitoring
Monitoring.DESCRIPTION: What this target is doing, as it does it. Readings arrive live; nothing is polled.
Monitoring.OFF_BODY: Sampling costs a round trip per interval whether anyone is watching or not, so it is off until you ask for it.
Monitoring.NO_DATA_BODY: This server has not reported this figure.
Monitoring.SLOWLOG_EMPTY_BODY: The server records a command here when it takes longer than its configured threshold.
Monitoring.DISCONNECT_BODY: Whatever is on the other end will lose its connection. It may reconnect on its own, or it may not.
Monitoring.BIG_KEYS_IDLE_BODY: Measuring costs one round trip per key, so it runs when you ask. A run looks at {{count}} keys.
Monitoring.BIG_KEYS_SAMPLED: Largest of {{sampled}} keys measured, holding {{total}} between them.
Monitoring.NO_CONNECTION_BODY: Open monitoring from a connection to watch it.

NotFound.TITLE: 404: Page not found
NotFound.DESCRIPTION: The page you requested does not exist.

Notifications.TITLE: Notifications
Notifications.EMPTY_BODY: Events from your targets appear here as they arrive.

Overview.TITLE: Overview
Overview.DESCRIPTION: Every target you have saved, at once.
Overview.EMPTY_BODY: Save a connection and this page will show every target you have, side by side.
Overview.ATTENTION_NONE_BODY: Every target is answering, no rule is firing, and the last of everything arranged to run did.

PubSub.TITLE: Pub/Sub
PubSub.DESCRIPTION: Watch channels and publish to them. The subscription belongs to the server, so every tab sees the same messages.
PubSub.SUBSCRIBE_FAILED: The subscription could not be opened
PubSub.FEED_EMPTY_LISTENING: The subscription is open; anything published to it appears here.
PubSub.FEED_EMPTY_IDLE: Subscribe to a channel to see messages arrive.
PubSub.NO_CONNECTION_BODY: Open pub/sub from a connection to watch its channels.

Schedules.TITLE: Scheduled work
Schedules.DESCRIPTION: Work that happens on its own — emptying a cache before a release, copying one environment over another every night, taking an export before a migration.
Schedules.EMPTY_BODY: A schedule is a job, a target and a cadence. Whatever is in a crontab and a shell script today can live here instead, where the credentials already are and where a run that stops is something you find out about.
Schedules.EMPTY_UNPRIVILEGED: Somebody with access to a server can arrange work on it. Ask for it on the one you need, and this page fills up.
Schedules.NO_MATCH_BODY: Change the search or the kind of work.
Schedules.LOAD_ERROR: The schedules could not be read
Schedules.NAME: Name
Schedules.NAME_HELP: What this is for, in the words you would use to explain why it exists.
Schedules.TARGET_HELP: Only the servers you may arrange this kind of work on are offered.
Schedules.NO_TARGETS_FOR_JOB: There is no server you may do this on. Access is granted per target, so ask for it on the one you need.
Schedules.REMOVE_BODY: “{{name}}” will stop running, and the record of what it did goes with it.
Schedules.ENABLED_HELP: Turn this off to keep the schedule without letting the clock start it. Running it by hand still works.
Schedules.DIALOG_INTRO: What to do, where, and how often. The permission is checked now and again every time it runs.
Schedules.JOB_FLUSH_DATABASE_HELP: Removes keys a batch at a time rather than with FLUSHDB, so a cache large enough to be worth emptying on a schedule does not block the server while it goes.
Schedules.JOB_COPY_KEYS_HELP: The same migration the key browser runs, started by the clock instead of by somebody.
Schedules.JOB_EXPORT_KEYS_HELP: A backup that needs no second server. The file is written where this deployment is configured to write exports.
Schedules.MATCH_HELP: A glob pattern. * means every key.
Schedules.DATABASE_HELP: Leave empty to use the one the connection is configured for.
Schedules.DESTINATION_HELP: A target cannot copy to itself.
Schedules.REPLACE: Overwrite keys that are already there
Schedules.REPLACE_HELP: Off means a key that already exists on the destination is left alone.
Schedules.MOVE: Remove each key from the source once it has arrived
Schedules.MOVE_HELP: This is a move rather than a copy. The source loses the keys.
Schedules.FILE_PREFIX_HELP: The start of the name; each run stamps the rest so nothing is overwritten.
Schedules.FILE_PREFIX_INVALID: A file name cannot contain a path.
Schedules.DAY_OF_MONTH_HELP: Stops at 28, because the 29th onwards is a day some months do not have.
Schedules.TIME_ZONE_HELP: The time zone is the one the Keydra server runs in.
Schedules.EXPRESSION_HELP: Ordinary five-field crontab syntax: minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week.
Schedules.SAYS_WITH_SCRIPT: {{says}}, with a script deciding each key
Schedules.SAYS_EXPORT: Writes keys matching {{match}} to a file named {{prefix}}…
Schedules.RUNS_FAILED: The history could not be read
Schedules.DESTINATION_PLACE_HELP: A destination configured under Backups. The credentials live there rather than on this schedule, so rotating a key is one edit.
Schedules.NO_DESTINATIONS: No destination is configured yet. An administrator sets one up under Backups, and this job cannot run without one.
Schedules.KEEP_LAST_HELP: Older backups written by this schedule are removed. Only this file name’s — another schedule’s history is left alone.

SecondFactor.TITLE: Second factor
SecondFactor.DESCRIPTION: An authenticator app asked for at every sign-in, so a stolen password is not enough on its own.
SecondFactor.SCAN: Scan this with your authenticator app, then type the code it shows to prove the pairing worked.
SecondFactor.QR_ALT: Pairing code for an authenticator app
SecondFactor.CONFIRM_HELP: Nothing changes until this is right, so a pairing you abandon costs nothing.
SecondFactor.CODES_BODY: Keep these somewhere other than the device with the authenticator on it. Each works once, and this is the only time they are shown — only their hashes are kept, so nothing here can show them again.
SecondFactor.CODES_RUNNING_OUT: You are running out of recovery codes
SecondFactor.CODES_RUNNING_OUT_BODY: Replace them now rather than after the last one is spent — without one, a lost authenticator is a lost account.
SecondFactor.REQUIRED_BODY: You are signed in, and there is nothing else you can reach until an authenticator is paired with your account. It takes a moment and you only do it once.
SecondFactor.REQUIRED_FAILED: The pairing could not be started. Try again, or sign out and back in.

Security.OPEN_HELP: This instance is not enforcing who may do what. Everyone who can reach it can do everything.

ServerAdmin.TITLE: Server settings
ServerAdmin.RUNNING: The server is writing right now.
ServerAdmin.SAVE_FAILED: The last save failed. Until it succeeds, a restart loses everything written since the last one that did.
ServerAdmin.NAME: Setting
ServerAdmin.PERSIST: Write these to the server’s file
ServerAdmin.RUNTIME_ONLY: A change takes effect at once and is forgotten on restart. Writing them to the server’s own file is the separate button above.
ServerAdmin.LOAD_ERROR: The settings could not be read
ServerAdmin.SNAPSHOT_FILE_HELP: On the server’s own filesystem — inside its container, if it runs in one. A snapshot is the server writing its memory to its disk, not a file Keydra can hand you.

Settings.COLOUR_SCHEME_HELP: Light or dark. Following the system changes with it, including on a schedule the system keeps.
Settings.CONFIRM_DESTRUCTIVE_HELP: Turning this off removes the confirmation on single deletions only. Clearing a namespace or a whole target always asks.
Settings.DESCRIPTION: Preferences that follow you rather than a target. Kept with your account, so they are the same wherever you sign in.
Settings.END_OTHERS_BODY: Every browser except this one will be signed out. Do this if you see a session you do not recognise.
Settings.END_SESSION_BODY: {{what}} will be signed out on its next request.
Settings.PAGE_SIZE_HELP: How many keys one scan returns. A larger page means fewer round trips and a longer wait for the first of them.
Settings.ROTATED_BODY: {{count}} stored secrets are now under key {{key}}.
Settings.ROTATION_HOW_BODY: Set the new secret as KEYDRA_SECRET_KEY, move the old one to KEYDRA_PREVIOUS_SECRET_KEYS, restart, press this, then remove the old one and restart again. The instance stays up throughout.
Settings.ROTATION_PENDING: Some secrets are still under a key that is only read
Settings.ROTATION_PENDING_BODY: Move them across, then take the old key out of the configuration and restart. That restart is the proof: anything missed would no longer decrypt.
Settings.SESSIONS_ERROR: Your sessions could not be read
Settings.SESSIONS_HELP: Every browser that can act as you right now. Ending one stops it on its next request.
Settings.SIGN_OUT_BODY: This is the browser you are reading on. You will need to sign in again.
Settings.SURFACE_HELP: High contrast strengthens every border and label. Glass draws panels as translucent, which is a look rather than an aid.
Settings.THEME_HELP: Felt is the theme PatternFly’s own documentation wears: red accents and pill-shaped controls.
Settings.TITLE: Settings
Settings.DESCRIPTION_LOCAL: Preferences that follow you rather than a target. Kept in this browser, because this instance has no accounts to keep them with.

SignIn.RETRYING: Keydra is being checked again every few seconds. This page continues on its own once the server answers.
SignIn.UNREACHABLE_BODY: The server is not answering. It may be starting up, or stopped.

SignIns.WATCH_DESCRIPTION: Sign-ins that did not look like the ones before them, and sign-ins that were refused. What people did once they were in is in the audit log.
SignIns.MINE_INTRO: How each of your sessions began, including the attempts that did not work. Every row here should be one you recognise.
SignIns.NOTHING_FLAGGED_BODY: Every sign-in in this window came from somewhere the account has been used before, on a browser it has been used on.
SignIns.NOTHING_REFUSED: No sign-in was refused in this window.
SignIns.LOAD_ERROR: Sign-in activity could not be loaded

Topology.TITLE: Topology
Topology.DESCRIPTION: How this target is arranged, and what it will let Keydra do.
Topology.NOT_DETECTED_BODY: This target would not say which commands it has, so everything is offered and an unsupported operation will fail where it is used.
Topology.SLOTS_UNCOVERED: {{missing}} of {{total}} slots are served by nobody — keys hashing to them cannot be read or written.
Topology.SLOT_BAR_LABEL: Which node serves each of the {{total}} hash slots
Topology.STANDALONE_BODY: This target is not clustered and is not a sentinel. There is nothing more to draw.
Topology.LOAD_ERROR: The arrangement could not be read
Topology.NO_CONNECTION_BODY: Open topology from a connection to see how it is arranged.
Topology.NOT_SERVING: This cluster is not serving requests
Topology.NOT_SERVING_BODY: The cluster reports a failed state, so reads and writes are refused whatever the node list below says. Look for a node the cluster has marked as gone, or for slots nobody owns.
Topology.UNASSIGNED_BODY: Keys hashing to them cannot be read or written. Assign them to a node, or add a node to take them.
Topology.SLOTS_FAILING_one: {{count}} slot is owned by a node the cluster believes has gone
Topology.SLOTS_FAILING_other: {{count}} slots are owned by a node the cluster believes has gone
Topology.SLOTS_FAILING_BODY: They are assigned, so the coverage bar shows them as served, and they are not being served. Bring that node back or let a replica take over.
Topology.NO_REPLICA_BODY: If one of those primaries goes, the slots it serves go with it and nothing can take over. Add a replica to each, or accept the loss knowingly.
Topology.RESHARDING_BODY: A reshard is running. Until it finishes, each of those slots is answered by one shard or the other and clients are redirected mid-request, so the shares below are halfway figures.

Tunnels.DESCRIPTION: The jump hosts things are reached through. Described once, pointed at from anywhere.
Tunnels.EMPTY_BODY: A target that is not reachable from where Keydra runs is the ordinary case in a production network, and a jump host is the ordinary answer. Describe one here and every target and backup destination behind it can point at it.
Tunnels.FINGERPRINT_HELP: Test the tunnel and the key it presented is offered here to be pinned.
Tunnels.INTRO: Where the jump host is, how to log in to it, and which host key it should present.
Tunnels.KEY_FILE_PLACEHOLDER: Choose a key file, or paste the key
Tunnels.LOAD_ERROR: The tunnels could not be read
Tunnels.NAME: Name
Tunnels.NAME_HELP: What people call this jump host, so a list of targets can say which one they go through.
Tunnels.NO_FINGERPRINT_BODY: Everything Keydra holds for everything behind this jump host travels through it, so anything that can answer on its address can have all of it. Test it and pin what it presents.
Tunnels.PRIVATE_KEY_HELP: Tried before the password when both are given. Stored encrypted, never written to disk.
Tunnels.PRIVATE_KEY_STORED: A key is stored. Leave this empty to keep it.
Tunnels.REMOVE_BODY: Keydra forgets how to reach “{{name}}”. Nothing points at it, so nothing loses its way there.
Tunnels.SAVE_FAILED: The tunnel could not be saved
Tunnels.SECRET_HELP: Leave empty to keep what is stored. Nothing can read a secret back to show it here.
Tunnels.SECRET_NEW_HELP: Stored encrypted, and never written to disk.
Tunnels.STORED: stored — leave empty to keep it
Tunnels.TEST_FAILED: The jump host could not be reached
Tunnels.TITLE: Tunnels

Value.COPIED_CLI: Value copied as a redis-cli command
Value.COPY_TRUNCATED: This value is only shown in part, so copying it would produce something shorter than what is stored.
Value.ENCODING_AUTO_HELP: Let the server detect the format
Value.GONE_BODY: It expired or was deleted after the list was built.
Value.LOAD_ERROR: The value could not be read
Value.TRUNCATED_HELP: The value is too large to return whole, so only the beginning is shown. It cannot be edited or copied from here without overwriting the rest.
Value.UNKNOWN_TYPE: This server returned a value type Keydra does not know how to show yet.
